about: Synastry aspects between two people born 1930–2009 (each birth a random day, 12:00 UT, from 1 January 1930 to 31 December 2009). orb: AGS's synastry orb for the pair (the wider body class: Sun and Moon 8°, Mercury, Venus and Mars 6°, Jupiter and Saturn 5°, Uranus, Neptune and Pluto 4°, Chiron, Lilith and the North Node 3°; times 1 for a conjunction or opposition, 0.85 for a trine or square, 0.6 for a sextile). personal: at least one of the two is the Sun, Moon, Mercury, Venus or Mars, the only contacts AGS's synastry readings count (two slow bodies are shared by everyone born in the same years). oneIn: about 1 pair of people in N has it, either way round (one person's first body with the other's second, or the reverse), counted on 3,000,000 random pairs; given only for personal pairs, where it holds whatever the age gap. birthdayGapDays (Sun, Mercury, Venus with themselves): the calendar gap between the two birthdays, any year, among pairs that have it (1st to 99th percentile, and the median). yearsApart (Mars and slower, with themselves): share of pairs born a given number of years apart that have it, in bins of binYears; likelyBands: the gaps at which at least half the pairs have it. examples (two slow bodies): for someone born on 1 July of the year shown, the birth months (1930–2009) of the people whose body makes the aspect with theirs. Positions from AGS's ephemeris: astronomy-engine (geocentric, true ecliptic of date), Chiron's integrated orbit, the true node, and the mean Black Moon Lilith (Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms, 2nd ed., ch. 47). birthdayGapDays (pairs of the Sun, Mercury and Venus, which stay close to the Sun): the calendar gap between the two birthdays, any year, among pairs that have it, either way round (1st to 99th percentile, and the median).
